_readme: DE-06 Non-Functional Design Agent config. Ensures production-grade quality — scalability, resilience, security, observability.

agent.name: Non-Functional Design Agent
agent.description: Analyses structured requirements and architecture context to produce non-functional requirement specifications (scalability, performance, availability, security, observability, resilience) and a security controls matrix.

behaviour._blocking_note: NFRs with critical or high priority that have confidence: low are blocking — must be resolved before downstream agents (e.g. Technology Selection, Hardening) consume the spec.

agent_network_html.description: Raw HTML content of the agent-network / business-process diagram. Drives service-boundary, integration-pattern, and threat-surface decisions — extract services, data flows, external interfaces, and trust boundaries from the embedded diagram and surrounding markup.

nfr_specifications.description: One item per non-functional requirement identified. Each item specifies category, target metric, threshold, and priority.

item_schema.category: scalability | performance | availability | security | observability | resilience
item_schema.target_metric: string — the measurable indicator (e.g. p95 latency, uptime %, RPS)
item_schema.rationale: string — why this threshold was chosen

security_controls.description: Security controls matrix covering authentication, authorization, encryption, network security, data protection, audit logging, and compliance mappings.

controls.domain: authentication | authorization | encryption | network_security | data_protection | audit_logging | compliance
controls.name: string

schema.threat_surface_summary: string — high-level summary of identified threat surfaces from agent_network_html

compliance_mappings.standard: string — e.g. SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR, PCI-DSS

scalability_design.description: Designs horizontal and vertical scaling strategies, capacity plans, load distribution patterns, and performance targets from SLA requirements and architecture context.

security_architecture.description: Defines security controls, threat mitigations, authentication/authorization patterns, encryption strategies, and compliance mappings based on trust boundaries extracted from the architecture.

observability_design.description: Designs logging, monitoring, distributed tracing, alerting rules, and SLO/SLI definitions to ensure production observability across all services.

resilience_design.description: Defines fault tolerance patterns (circuit breakers, retries, bulkheads), disaster recovery objectives (RPO/RTO), and degradation strategies for each service boundary.

compliance_mapping._note: Deferred. Would map security controls to specific regulatory frameworks (SOC2, ISO27001, PCI-DSS) with evidence requirements per control.

load_modeler.description: Models expected load patterns, peak traffic, and capacity requirements from structured_requirements volume/throughput hints and service topology from agent_network_html.

security_scanner.description: Scans the architecture topology (from agent_network_html) for security vulnerabilities — exposed interfaces, missing encryption boundaries, unprotected data flows.

slo_definer.description: Derives SLOs and SLIs from SLA requirements in structured_requirements. Calculates error budgets and alerting thresholds per service.

git_reader._enabled_note: false → read from local files under tech_stack.git_reader.local_audit_dir. true → read from the real audit repo via GitPython. Toggle per environment.
git_reader._note: run_id is passed by GenWiz as X-Run-ID header on every agent call. Agent uses it to resolve the path and read previous step output.

dev._note: Used only when ENV=dev AND enabled=true. phase_input_fixture replaces an empty HTTP body. git_input_fixtures override the git/local fetch for the listed fields. phase_input_text_files load raw text files (HTML/MD/TXT) into the listed payload fields. In prod (ENV=prod) this whole block is ignored.
